title: Why your suction line is frosting over
takeaway: Frost alone doesn't prove floodback - measure the superheat before condemning anything.

payoff.line2: The number tells you - not the ice.

sentences: Here's why your suction line is frosting over.
shots.visual: the frosted suction line itself, ice already formed from the evaporator outlet toward the compressor

sentences: When airflow is low or the system is overfed, refrigerant is still boiling as it leaves the coil, and the line runs colder than it should.
captions: Low airflow — or an overfed coil
Still boiling as it leaves the coil
shots.visual: camera travels the flow: liquid enters through the TXV at bottom-left, boils across the passes, droplets still surviving at the top-right outlet

sentences: Below freezing, moisture in the air freezes onto the pipe — that's your frost.
captions: Moisture in the air freezes onto the pipe
shots.visual: the suction line begins at the outlet coupling; it chills toward icy pale and frost accumulates from the outlet toward the compressor

sentences: But frost alone doesn't prove liquid floodback.
captions: Frost alone doesn't prove liquid floodback
shots.visual: pull out: coil, frosted line and compressor context in one frame

sentences: The number tells you — not the ice.
shots.visual: open on the temperature clamp just past the outlet, highlight ring pulsing, then pull until TXV, coil, line and compressor share the frame
